Let $A, B, C$ be posets and let $f : C \times A \to B$ be a poset morphism. Writing $\mathsf{curry}(f) : C \to (A \rightharpoonup B)$ for the curried form of $f$, $\mathsf{eval} : (A \rightharpoonup B) \times A \to B$ for the evaluation morphism, and $- \times_1 \mathsf{id}$ for the functorial action on morphisms of the binary product, the composite
$$\mathsf{eval} \circ (\mathsf{curry}(f) \times_1 \mathsf{id}_A)$$
is pointwise equal to $f$. This is the $\beta$-reduction (counit) law of the exponential adjunction in the category of posets, where $A \rightharpoonup B$ denotes the function poset (exponential object) on order-preserving maps ordered pointwise.

-- The pointwise partial order on order preserving maps.

-- exponential/hom object based on this order.)

module Pointwise {A : Poset a₁ a₂ a₃} {B : Poset b₁ b₂ b₃} where

  infix 4 _≤°_

  _≤°_ : (f g : A ⇒ B) → Set (a₁ ⊔ b₃)
  f ≤° g = ∀ {x} → ₍ B ₎ ⟦ f ⟧ x ≤ ⟦ g ⟧ x

  ≤°-isPartialOrder : IsPartialOrder _≗_ _≤°_

    { isPreorder      = record
      { isEquivalence = ≗-isEquivalence

      ; trans         = λ f≤g g≤h → trans B f≤g g≤h
      }
    ; antisym         = λ f≤g g≤f → antisym B f≤g g≤f
